rules: Chapter 4: Traffic Control
Right on red in New York City
Wait for green unless a sign allows the turn. Outside New York City, the default rule allows a right turn after stopping and yielding unless a sign prohibits it.
You're in Queens at a steady red with no turn-on-red sign. The crosswalk and traffic are clear. Can you turn right?
Wait for green.
You're outside New York City, stopped at a steady red without a turn restriction. Can you turn now if you have yielded and it is clear?
Yes, if it is safe.
Chapter 6: Passing, School Buses
School bus on a divided highway
Drivers on both sides must stop for a school bus with its red lights flashing, even on a divided highway. Stop at least 20 feet from the bus.
An approaching school bus stops with red lights flashing across a grassy median. Can you keep going?
No. Stop.
You follow a school bus that stops with its red lights on. Is stopping one car length away always enough?
No. Leave at least 20 feet.
Chapter 1: Driver Licenses
Permit supervision
A learner needs a licensed supervising driver at least 21 years old, qualified for the vehicle. Junior permit rules also vary by part of the state.
Your 20-year-old sibling has a full license. Can they be your only supervisor?
No. They are too young to supervise.
A 25-year-old has only a motorcycle license. Can they supervise your car practice?
No. They need a license valid for the vehicle.
Chapter 6: Passing
Passing cyclists and using the shoulder
Pass a bicyclist on the left at a safe distance. Do not use the shoulder as a passing lane unless directed by a traffic officer or allowed by a sign.
There is no clear gap to the left of a cyclist, but the paved shoulder is empty. Can you pass on the shoulder?
No. Wait for a safe pass on the left.
You've moved left around a cyclist, but your rear bumper is still next to the bicycle. Can you move right?
No. Clear the cyclist before returning.
Chapter 1: Driver Licenses, Regional Restrictions for a Junior Permit
Junior permit practice in New York City
In the five boroughs, junior permit practice requires dual brakes and a qualifying supervisor such as a licensed parent or instructor. Junior permit driving is not allowed there from 9 p.m. to 5 a.m.
A qualifying instructor meets you in Brooklyn at noon, but the car has no instructor's brake. Can you practice in it?
No. The vehicle must have dual controls.
Your licensed parent has arranged a dual-control car at 9:30 p.m. in Manhattan. Is it legal for you to practice with a junior permit?
No. The city nighttime restriction still applies.

Learner license age and school documents
The teen path starts at 15. Bring proof of driver education and eligibility from school or proof of graduation or its equivalent.

rules: Chapter 1: Your License to Drive
Who rides with a Texas learner
The licensed supervising adult must be at least 21 and sit in the front passenger seat.
Your licensed 19-year-old cousin offers to supervise you. Can you drive with only them?
No. Find a licensed adult who is at least 21.
Your eligible supervisor sits in the back while a friend sits in front. What needs to change?
Move the supervising driver to the front passenger seat.
Chapter 1: Your License to Drive
No phone use on a learner license
Learner license holders cannot use a phone while driving, including hands-free calls, except in an emergency.
You want to confirm dinner plans using the car's hands-free system while you drive. Is that allowed?
No. Wait until you are safely stopped.
A friend says the learner phone restriction only applies if you touch the screen. Is that right?
No. Ordinary hands-free use is also restricted.
Chapter 4: Right-of-Way
Buses on separate roadways

If the opposite side is separated by a physical barrier or intervening space, the opposite-direction driver does not have to stop. Painted lines or a shared left-turn lane do not make two separate roadways.
A bus across a painted center turn lane flashes red. Does the painted lane let you continue?
No. Stop.
The bus is across a physical median on a separate roadway. You are going the other direction. Does the Texas bus stop rule require a stop?
Not on that separate roadway; stay alert for people crossing.
Chapter 6: Signaling, Passing, and Turning
Signal before the corner
Texas requires the turn signal continuously for at least the last 100 feet before turning.
You start your signal only when the front tires reach the corner. What was missed?
The advance signal before the turn.
The right lane bends; your signal has been on for 50 feet and you are about to turn into a side street. Is that enough?
No. Signal for at least the last 100 feet.
Chapter 6: Signaling, Passing, and Turning
No left-side pass near crossings
Do not drive left of center to pass within 100 feet of an intersection or railroad crossing.
A slow truck is 70 feet before a crossing and the opposing lane is empty. Can you pass left of center?
No. Wait until you are out of the restricted area and passing is safe.
You approach an intersection 80 feet away behind a slow car. Does a gap in oncoming traffic make a left-side pass legal there?
No. The intersection distance still applies.

manual: Official Florida Driver License Handbook, English edition (FLHSMV)
facts: Multiple-choice Class E exam on traffic laws, safe driving, and traffic controls.
next: Florida learner license law and supervision rules
links: Class E and first-time driver education
rules: Getting Your License: Learner's License
Daylight first, then a later cutoff
For the first three months a Florida learner may drive only in daylight. After that, supervised driving can continue until 10 p.m.
You got your learner's license last month. Can you practice after sunset if a supervisor rides along?
No. The first three months are daylight only.
You've held the learner's license four months. With proper supervision, can you drive home at 9:30 p.m.?
Yes, if you finish before the 10 p.m. cutoff.
Getting Your License: Learner's License
Supervision in the front passenger seat
A driver with a valid license who is at least 21 must sit in the closest seat to the learner's right.
An adult with a license sits in the back while your sibling occupies the front passenger seat. May you start?
No. The qualified driver needs to sit beside you.
The person beside you is 20 and fully licensed. Can they be your learner supervisor?
No. Find a licensed driver who is at least 21.
Sharing the Road: School Buses
The median matters for an oncoming school bus
In the opposite direction you can continue with caution if a raised barrier or an unpaved median at least five feet wide separates traffic. A painted median does not count.
A school bus flashes red on the far side of a painted median. Can you proceed?
No. Stop.
An oncoming school bus is stopped across a raised concrete barrier. Must you stop for its signal?
No, but continue cautiously and watch for children.
Getting Your License: Class E Knowledge Exam
Account for the full Class E exam
Road signs are only one part of the Class E knowledge exam. A sign-only practice score does not include traffic laws or safe driving.
You recognize all your flashcards. What should you study next before booking the Class E test?
Traffic laws and safe-driving decisions as well as sign recognition.
You missed 11 questions on a 50-question practice set. Have you reached Florida's 40-correct mark?
No. That is 39 correct.
Traffic Controls: Traffic Signals
Right turns at a steady red signal
Where a sign does not prohibit it, stop completely and yield to pedestrians and conflicting traffic before turning right on a steady red.
You've stopped at a red light, but a pedestrian has begun crossing your intended path. What do you do?
Wait until the crossing is clear and the turn is safe.
The street is empty, but a sign prohibits turns on red. Can you turn after stopping?
No. Wait for a signal that permits the turn.

facts: Schedule the written knowledge test after purchasing a permit. MVC lists written languages and English and Spanish oral tests.
Wait seven days after failing the knowledge test.

next: New Jersey MVC first license steps
rules: Chapter 1: The New Jersey Driver License System
Red GDL decals
GDL drivers under 21 must display the MVC red reflective decals on the front and rear plates.
You are 17 and your practice car has the decal only on the rear plate. Is it ready?
No. Display both decals.
You borrow a second car for the road test. Does the decal on your usual practice car count?
No. Display the required decals on the car you use.
Chapter 1: The New Jersey Driver License System
Supervising driver experience
Your front-seat supervisor must be at least 21, hold a valid New Jersey license, and have at least three years of driving experience.
Your 22-year-old neighbor has held their first license for two years. Can they supervise?
No. The experience requirement is at least three years.
A licensed driver from another state has decades of experience. Does their out-of-state license satisfy the MVC supervisor rule?
No. The required license is a valid New Jersey license.
Chapter 1: The New Jersey Driver License System
Nighttime hours for under-21 GDL drivers
The normal restricted period is 11:01 p.m. to 5 a.m. An applicable MVC exemption may change the rule; don't assume a late errand is exempt.
You're 17 and plan to begin an ordinary practice drive at midnight. Does having a supervisor make the trip allowable?
No. Midnight is inside the restricted period.
A 19-year-old probationary driver wants to leave at 4:45 a.m. for a social trip. May they drive?
No. The ordinary restriction runs until 5 a.m.
Chapter 1: The New Jersey Driver License System
Phone use under GDL
A special learner permit holder cannot use a handheld or hands-free phone while driving. Set up directions and calls before departure.
A learner connects a hands-free headset to answer a call on the road. Does that meet MVC rules?
No. Hands-free phone use is restricted too.
You want to call a friend to say you're running late. When should you make the call?
Before driving or after safely parking.
Chapter 1: The New Jersey Driver License System
Supervised practice for a permit issued under age 21
For permits issued on or after February 1, 2025 to drivers under 21, the MVC requires 50 supervised hours, including 10 in darkness, before a probationary license.
You logged 52 hours but only eight at night. Is the practice record complete?
No. Log at least two more hours in darkness.
You logged 40 daylight hours and 10 after dark. Have you met both counts?
Yes. This meets the hour requirements, not the other licensing requirements.

signs: Section 7: Laws and Rules of the Road
facts: Multiple-choice knowledge test. The DMV publishes an 80% passing score.
The minor instruction-permit path begins at 15½. Bring education documents as applicable and check the DMV's identity and residency requirements.
After a failed knowledge test, a minor must wait seven days, not counting the day of the failure.
rules: Section 2: Getting an Instruction Permit and Driver's License
Permit holding period for minors
A driver under 18 generally must hold an instruction permit at least six months before scheduling the behind-the-wheel test, unless they turn 18 first.
You are 17 and have held your permit for five months. Does finishing your lessons let you schedule the drive test now?
No. Meet the holding-period requirement as well.
You turn 18 while still holding a permit issued four months ago. Does the minor holding period still apply?
No. Check the adult application path for the remaining requirements.
Section 2: Getting an Instruction Permit and Driver's License
Provisional nighttime restriction
During the first year of a minor's provisional license, ordinary driving between 11 p.m. and 5 a.m. is restricted. Exceptions require a qualifying purpose and supporting documentation.
You're 17, newly licensed, and want to drive to a friend's house at midnight. Is that ordinarily allowed?
No. That is during the restricted period.
A coach says a late school trip is automatically exempt. What should you check?
Whether the school exception applies and whether you have the required signed note.
Section 2: Getting an Instruction Permit and Driver's License
Young passengers on a provisional license
The minor provisional restrictions normally bar passengers under 20 in the first year without a qualifying accompanying driver or a documented exception.
At 17, can you drive two 18-year-old friends to the store with only your provisional license?
No, not without a qualifying supervisor or exception.
A California-licensed parent will ride with you and a 16-year-old passenger. Is the young-passenger restriction the same as if you drove alone?
No. A qualifying accompanying parent changes the result.
Section 7: Laws and Rules of the Road
Blue and red curbs
A blue curb is reserved for qualifying vehicles displaying a disabled-parking placard or plate. A red curb prohibits an ordinary driver from stopping, standing, or parking.
You do not have a disabled placard or plate. The blue curb is empty and your passenger needs only a minute. Can you park there?
No. The space is reserved.
A red curb is the shortest place to pick up your friend. May you stop there without parking?
No. Go to a lawful pickup location.
Section 7: Laws and Rules of the Road
Passing someone on a bicycle
Change lanes to pass a bicyclist when possible. If you cannot change lanes, leave at least three feet; if that gap is not safe, wait.
The road has a clear lane to your left and a cyclist ahead. What should you do when safe?
Change lanes to pass.
An oncoming car blocks the only space needed to leave three feet. What is the right choice?
Wait behind the bicycle until you can pass safely.

signs: Traffic Signs, Signals and Pavement Markings
facts: At least 35 Class D questions; 80% correct. English is required to be available; the Secretary of State may offer additional languages.
Study signs, signals, pavement markings, multiple-choice items and true-or-false items.
The graduated licensing permit phase starts at age 15.
rules: Chapter 4: Traffic Laws, Speed Limits
Signed school-zone speed limit
The 20 mph rule applies on school days between 6:30 a.m. and 4 p.m. when children are present and signs are posted.
Children are outside a signed school zone at 3 p.m. on a school day. Is the usual road speed the limit there?
No. The school-zone limit is 20 mph.
You see a posted school-zone sign after school hours. Can that time alone tell you every applicable limit?
No. Check posted instructions and conditions; the specific school-zone rule has several conditions.
Chapter 3: Drivers Under Age 21
Permit holding period
The Illinois teen permit generally must be held for at least nine months before moving to initial licensing, alongside other GDL requirements.
You got the permit at 15 and have held it seven months. Are you through the holding phase?
No. The minimum is nine months.
Nine months have passed, but you have not finished supervised practice. Are you ready simply because enough time elapsed?
No. The hours are a separate requirement.
Chapter 3: Drivers Under Age 21
Supervised practice hours
A teen needs at least 50 practice hours, including 10 at night, with a qualifying supervisor.
Your log has 51 hours, seven of them at night. What is missing?
Three nighttime hours.
Your log has 39 daylight hours and 10 nighttime hours. Does it satisfy both counts?
No. One more total hour is needed.
Chapter 3: Drivers Under Age 21
Hands-free phone restriction under 19
Drivers under age 19 cannot use a phone while driving, including hands-free, except for an eligible emergency contact.
You're 18 and want to dictate a routine text with voice controls. Is it allowed?
No. Hands-free use is also restricted.
A driver under 19 needs emergency services after seeing a crash. Is that the same as using a phone for a social call?
No. The rule includes an emergency exception.
Chapter 3: Drivers Under Age 21
Weeknight and weekend restrictions
The statewide GDL limit normally starts at 10 p.m. Sunday through Thursday and 11 p.m. Friday and Saturday. Local curfews can differ.
A teen with an initial license plans an ordinary Thursday drive at 10:30 p.m. Is it within ordinary hours?
No. The Thursday restriction starts at 10 p.m.
Does the same 10 p.m. statewide start automatically apply on Saturday?
No. Saturday's statewide start is 11 p.m.; local rules can be earlier.

signs: Chapter 2: Signs, Signals and Pavement Markings
facts: Multiple-choice knowledge test. PennDOT lists written and audio options in its testing guide.
Bring the completed DL-180 including a medical examination, identification and applicable residency evidence. Minor applicants also need DL-180TD.
rules: Chapter 3: Learning to Drive, School Buses
School bus stop distance and barriers
Stop at least 10 feet from a bus flashing red with its arm out. You do not need to stop on a separate roadway divided by a physical barrier when traveling in the opposite direction.
You follow a school bus and it activates red lights and extends its arm. Is stopping five feet behind it enough?
No. Stop at least 10 feet back.
The red lights are on and you are opposite the bus across a painted turn lane. Does the paint exempt you from stopping?
No. A painted lane is not a physical barrier.
Chapter 1: Non-Commercial Learner's Permit Information
Practice hours include night and poor weather
Applicants under 18 must complete 65 practice hours with at least 10 at night and five in poor weather.
You've logged 65 hours, including the nighttime minimum but no bad-weather practice. Is the log ready?
No. The poor-weather hours are a separate requirement.
There are 65 hours, five in poor weather, but only nine at night. What do you add?
At least one more nighttime hour.
Chapter 1: Non-Commercial Learner's Permit Information
Who can supervise a learner
A licensed supervisor ordinarily must be at least 21, but the listed parent, guardian, person in loco parentis or spouse exception starts at 18.
Your 20-year-old licensed cousin is not your guardian. Can they be your only supervisor?
No. They are under 21 and do not fit a listed exception.
Can your 20-year-old licensed spouse meet the supervisor age requirement?
Yes. A licensed spouse can qualify from age 18.
Chapter 3: Learning to Drive, Work Zones
Headlights in signed work zones
Use your headlights as required through posted work zones. Daytime running lights are not a substitute.
You enter a signed active work zone on a bright day. Are daytime running lights enough?
No. Use your headlights.
Cars around you have not switched their lights on in a signed work zone. Does that change your obligation?
No. Turn on your headlights.
Chapter 1: Non-Commercial Learner's Permit Information
Learner nighttime supervision
Between 11 p.m. and 5 a.m. a learner needs a parent, guardian, person in loco parentis or spouse who meets the licensing and age requirement.
Your 23-year-old friend usually supervises you. Can they be your only supervisor at midnight?
No. The learner nighttime rule is narrower.
At 4:30 a.m., can a qualifying licensed parent supervise instead?
Yes, if the parent meets the stated requirements.

manual: What Every Driver Must Know (SOS-133), November 2026 edition
signs: Part 2: Learn the rules of the road
facts: The separate Segment 1 driver education exam requires at least 70%. Do not use that grade as the adult knowledge test passing rule.
First-time adults take the SOS knowledge test at an office or, for eligible customers, online.
Level 1 starts at 14 years and 9 months after Segment 1 and the other application steps.
links: Adult Michigan test and Temporary Instruction Permit
rules: Part 1: Before you drive, Teen licensing
Separate course and license ages
Segment 1 enrollment starts at 14 years and 8 months; a Level 1 license requires at least 14 years and 9 months plus the required steps.
You just turned 14 years and 8 months. Can you start driver education?
Yes, you meet the Segment 1 enrollment age.
Can you start private supervised practice with a Level 1 license before reaching 14 years and 9 months?
No. Course eligibility is not license eligibility.
Part 1: Before you drive, Teen licensing
Supervision requires authorization
With a Level 1 license, drive with a parent, guardian or designated licensed adult who meets the state's requirements. An otherwise qualified adult friend is not automatically designated.
Your parent has not designated the licensed adult who volunteered to supervise. Can you treat that volunteer as your supervisor?
No. Make sure your parent or guardian designates the qualified adult first.
A designated licensed adult is only 20. Is designation alone enough?
No. That adult must also be at least 21.
Part 1: Before you drive, Teen licensing
Segment 2 prerequisites
Before Segment 2, hold Level 1 for three consecutive months and log at least 30 practice hours, including two at night.
You completed 35 hours but have held Level 1 for only two months. Can you start Segment 2?
No. The license holding period is separate.
Your three months are up and you logged 30 daylight hours. Is your log ready?
No. It must include at least two hours at night.
Part 2: Learn the rules of the road, When a school bus stops
Michigan school bus clearance
Stop at least 20 feet away when the bus's overhead reds flash on an undivided road. Opposite traffic on a genuinely separated roadway can be exempt; take care near a crosswalk.
A stopped bus across a solid painted yellow line activates its overhead reds. When do you stop?
Stop at least 20 feet from the bus.
You are following directly behind the bus and it activates its overhead reds. Can you drive around it because the other lane is empty?
No. Stop and remain stopped while its red warning is active.
Part 2: Learn the rules of the road, Turns and intersections
How a Michigan Left works
Where a direct left is prohibited, follow the signs for the median crossover. A Michigan Left uses that designated opening, not any gap in the median.
You want to turn left at a junction but the approach has a No Left Turn sign and signed crossover arrows. What is your next step?
Follow the crossover route instead of turning directly left.
You missed the designated crossover and see an unsigned break in a raised median. Do you treat it as the same route?
No. Continue to a lawful, signed route.
